source.title: MiniGPT: Rebuilding GPT from First Principles

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports held-out validation losses for two differently sized language-model configurations, providing a limited conceptual comparison relevant to the size–loss direction. It does not fit or test scaling laws.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling-law work but does not evaluate power-law fits, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocation. Its two model configurations differ in context length and training settings as well as parameter count. The validation-loss measurements are recorded, but they cannot establish a power-law relationship.
record.test_reason: MiniGPT is an implementation report. It trains two differently configured character-level models on Tiny Shakespeare. Parameters, context length, batch size, schedule, regularization and checkpoint selection all change together. No scaling sweep, power-law fit, extrapolation or allocation analysis is done. Kaplan and Hoffmann are cited only in the limitations section. Two confounded points cannot bear on any version, so the study does not test the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors frame MiniGPT as a reproducible implementation study, not a scaling test. They report that the stronger configuration improved best validation loss to 1.4780. They attribute the gain jointly to capacity, context, regularization, scheduling and checkpoint selection, and note overfitting after step 1750.
record.recipe_differences: The paper trains two small character-level Tiny Shakespeare models and reports validation losses; it does not use the original studies' scaling sweeps, power-law fitting, or compute-allocation method.
record.method_sensitivity: The two configurations also differ in context length, architecture, batch size, training schedule, regularization, and checkpoint selection. For the stronger model, validation loss differs by training step: 1.4780 at step 1750 and 1.7055 at step 5000.
record.problems: Only two configurations are reported, with multiple settings changing together; the dataset and models are small; there is no scaling-law fit, compute or token sweep, or uncertainty estimate. The paper itself notes overfitting in the stronger run.
record.rows_left_out: Training losses and qualitative generation results were left out because the claim versions concern held-out pretraining loss, scaling, and downstream predictability; the paper reports no downstream task results.

untested.parts: No sweep or power-law fit over parameters, tokens or compute.
Shape is not varied at fixed parameter count.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and V1 links are overcalls. The paper explicitly does not focus on scale and mentions scaling laws only as a limitation.

versions.untested_parts: Only two configurations are compared. The paper does not fit a power law, cover several orders of magnitude, isolate parameter count from other settings, or test loss scaling with tokens or compute.
No predictions fitted on small runs are compared with substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or parameter/token scaling trend is tested.
Depth, width, and other architecture choices are not varied at fixed parameter count.
No other modality, repeated-data regime, fine-tuning, or transfer setting is tested.
No scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal split are fitted or compared across fitting choices.

rows.subject: Baseline MiniGPT
rows.operation_detail: Compared with a separately configured larger run; no controlled scaling sweep.
rows.note: This is one of two differently configured runs, not a power-law fit.
rows.check: This is a single run used to verify the pipeline, not a scaling measurement. It has no link to a power-law version.

rows.subject: Stronger MiniGPT
rows.operation_detail: Compared with a separately configured smaller run; no controlled scaling sweep.
rows.note: The stronger run also changes context length, architecture, regularization, learning-rate schedule, and checkpoint selection; the comparison does not isolate parameter count or establish a power law.
rows.check: The size jump (0.83M to 10.77M) is confounded with context length, batch, LR schedule, dropout and best-checkpoint selection. The authors attribute the gain to all of these together, so this is not a scaling row.

rows.subject: Stronger MiniGPT
rows.operation_detail: Validation loss reported at the final training step of the stronger run.
rows.note: The paper says validation loss rises after step 1750 while training loss continues to fall, describing this as overfitting. This is not a fitted loss-versus-token scaling curve.
rows.check: This row shows overfitting within one run on a tiny dataset (best vs final checkpoint). It is not a loss-versus-tokens or compute scaling measurement.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
